sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 26.0% a year from $4,319 million in FY2016 to $34,639 million in FY2025 [F1][F10][F231].
The path was a step change rather than a smooth climb: revenue rose 68.3% in FY2021 and 43.6% in FY2022, then fell 3.9% in FY2023 before recovering 13.7% and 34.3% [D258][D314][D370][D426][D483].
The FY2022 jump included the Xilinx acquisition, which lifted Embedded revenue from $246 million to $4,552 million [S109][S110][P41].
The FY2023 decline came from a 25% fall in Client revenue on weak PC demand and inventory correction, partly offset by Embedded [P35].
FY2025 growth was driven by Data Center and Client and Gaming, with Data Center revenue up 32% on EPYC processors and Instinct GPUs [P15][P13].
Data Center is now the largest segment at 48.0% of revenue and contributed 15.7pp of the 34.3% FY2025 growth [D692][D694][D483].
Client and Gaming contributed 19.0pp in FY2025, with Client revenue up 51% on a 31% rise in processor units and a 15% rise in average selling price [D701][P10].
Gaming revenue rose 51% on higher semi-custom revenue and Radeon GPU demand, while Embedded fell 3% as end-market demand stayed mixed [P9][P15].
Operating income grew 94.4% against 34.3% revenue growth, an incremental operating margin of 20.3% [D484][D483][D511].
Diluted EPS grew 165.0% against 164.2% net income growth, with the diluted share count essentially flat at -0.1% [D487][D485][D506].
Operating margin of 10.7% in FY2025 sits above the 7.2% window median but far below the 22.2% FY2021 high [F60][D795][D794].
Gross margin reached a window high of 49.5%, up 0.2pp, against a 44.7% median [F40][D498][D801].
The gross margin gain came from product mix, partly offset by about $440 million of MI308 inventory and export-control charges [P14].
In the FY2025 bridge, cost of revenue added 0.2pp, R&D added 1.7pp, and SG&A cost 1.2pp as it grew 48.9% [D513][D514][D515][D503].
Net margin of 12.5% exceeded operating margin because other income of $577 million rose on unrealized investment gains and the tax line was a $103 million benefit [F80][F60][P5][P4].
Operating cash flow of $7,709 million and free cash flow of $6,735 million were 1.78x and 1.55x net income, against a 1.17x window median for free cash flow [F110][F130][D470][D471][D810].
Free cash flow margin of 19.4% matched the FY2021 high of 19.6% and far exceeded the 6.5% median [D467][D803][D804].
Operating cash flow was reduced by a $2.2 billion inventory build to support Data Center product ramps [P3].
Capex of $974 million was 2.8% of revenue and 1.87x D&A, the highest ratio in the window [F120][D466][D472].
Net cash rose to $6,456 million, or 18.6% of revenue, the 100th percentile against six semis peers whose median is -13.9% [D476][D477][D826][D827].
Total debt rose 138% to $4,096 million after $1.5 billion of notes were issued in March 2025, lifting interest expense to $131 million [D475][D508][P6][F93].
Buybacks of $1,316 million were 19.5% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count fell 0.1% [X150][D479][D506].
Return on average equity of 7.2% ranks at the 17th percentile against a 26.7% peer median [D482][D830][D831].
Operating margin of 10.7% is 20.3pp below the 31.0% semis peer median, ranking 17th percentile, despite the revenue scale [F60][D819][D818].
Total debt rose 138% in FY2025 to $4,096 million, though net cash still rose to $6,456 million [D475][D508][D476].
Days inventory outstanding climbed to 165 days from 160, extending a build from 106 days in FY2022 [D481][D424][D312].
The FY2025 tax benefit of $103 million included an $853 million release of uncertain tax positions, so the -2.5% effective rate is not repeatable [P4][D469].
Watch operating margin against the 7.2% window median; a print below it would reverse the FY2025 recovery [D795][F60].
Watch days inventory outstanding against the FY2025 level of 165 days; a further rise would signal demand lagging the build [D481].
Watch Data Center segment operating margin against its FY2025 21.7%, down from 27.7% in FY2024, in the next 10-K [D769][D768].
